text: This Act has the purpose of protecting the personality and fundamental rights of natural persons whose personal data is processed.

text: This Act applies to the processing of personal data of natural persons by:

text: The applicable procedural law regulates the processing of personal data and the data subject's rights in court proceedings and in proceedings governed by federal procedural regulations. This Act applies to first instance administrative proceedings.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The public registers for private legal transactions, and in particular the access to these registers and the data subject's rights, shall be regulated by the specific provisions of the applicable federal law. If the specific provisions do not contain any rules, this Act applies.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: This Act applies to circumstances that have an effect in Switzerland, even if they were initiated abroad.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: For rights under private law, the Federal Act of 18 December 1987 on Private International Law applies. In addition, the provisions on the territorial scope of application of the Criminal Code are reserved.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC) supervises the application of the federal data protection regulations.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The following are exempted from supervision by the FDPIC:

text: In this Act:

text: Personal data must be processed lawfully.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The processing must be carried out in good faith and be proportionate.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: Personal data may only be collected for a specific purpose that the data subject can recognise; personal data may only be further processed in a manner that is compatible with this purpose.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: They shall be destroyed or anonymised as soon as they are no longer required for the purpose of processing.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: Any person who processes personal data must satisfy themselves that the data are accurate. They must take all appropriate measures to correct, delete or destroy data that are incorrect or incomplete insofar as the purpose for which they are collected or processed is concerned. The appropriateness of the measures depends in particular on the form and the extent of the processing and on the risk that the processing poses to the data subject's personality or fundamental rights.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: If the consent of the data subject is required, such consent is only valid if given voluntarily for one or more specific instances of processing based on appropriate information.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The consent must be explicitly given for:
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The controller is obliged to arrange the data processing in technical and organisational terms so that the data protection regulations, and in particular the principles under Article 6, are respected. It shall take account of this from the planning stage.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The technical and organisational measures must in particular be appropriate with regard to the state of the art, the nature and the extent of the data processing and the risk that the processing poses to the data subject's personality or fundamental rights.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The controller is obliged to ensure by means of suitable default settings that the processing of personal data is limited to the minimum required for the purpose intended, unless the data subject specifies otherwise.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The controller and the processor shall guarantee a level of data security appropriate to the risk by taking suitable technical and organisational measures.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The measures must make it possible to avoid breaches of data security.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The Federal Council shall issue provisions on the minimum requirements for data security.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The processing of personal data may be assigned by contract or by the legislation to a processor if:
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The controller must satisfy itself in particular that the processor is able to guarantee data security.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The processor may only assign processing to a third party with prior approval from the controller.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: It may claim the same grounds for justification as the controller.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: Private controllers may appoint a data protection officer.

text: The Federal Council shall regulate the appointment of data protection officers by federal bodies.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: Professional, industry and trade associations that are authorised to safeguard the economic interests of their members in their articles of association and federal bodies may submit codes of conduct to the FDPIC.

text: The FDPIC shall state and publish his or her opinions on the codes of conduct.

text: The Federal Council shall issue regulations on the recognition of certification procedures and the introduction of a data protection quality mark. In doing so, it shall take account of international law and the internationally recognised technical standards.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: If processing is likely to result in a high risk to the data subject's personality or fundamental rights, the controller shall carry out a data protection impact assessment beforehand. If several similar processing procedures are planned, a joint assessment may be carried out.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The existence of a high risk, in particular when using new technologies, depends on the nature, extent, circumstances and purpose of the processing. A high risk arises in particular:
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The data protection impact assessment shall include a description of the planned processing, an evaluation of the risks to the data subject's personality or fundamental rights and a description of the measures to protect personality and fundamental rights.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: Private controllers are exempt from having to carry out a data protection impact assessment if they are required by law to process the data.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: A private controller may dispense with carrying out a data protection impact assessment if it uses a system, product or service that is certified under Article 13 for the intended use, or if it complies with a code of conduct under Article 11 that satisfies the following requirements:

text: If the data protection impact assessment indicates that the planned processing despite the measures planned by the controller will still pose a high risk to the personality or the data subject's fundamental rights, the controller shall seek the FDPIC's opinion beforehand.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The FDPIC shall inform the controller within two months of any objections to the planned processing. This deadline may be extended by one month if the data processing is complex.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: If the FDPIC objects to the planned processing, he or she shall propose suitable measures to the controller.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: A private controller may dispense with consulting the FDPIC if it has consulted the data protection officer under Article 10.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The controller shall notify the FDPIC of any breach of data security that is likely to lead to a high risk to the data subject's personality or fundamental rights as quickly as possible.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: In the notification, it shall as a minimum specify the nature of the breach of data security, its consequences and the measures taken or planned.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The processor shall notify the controller of any breach of data security as quickly as possible.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The Commissioner may not have any additional occupations.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The Judicial Committee may permit the Commissioner to carry out an additional occupation provided this does not adversely affect the exercise of his or her duties or the independence and the reputation of the FDPIC. The decision shall be published.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: In the event of any dispute with regard to the Commissioner's recusal, the decision shall be taken by the president of the division of the Federal Administrative Court that is competent in data protection matters.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The FDPIC shall ensure by means of suitable control measures, in particular in relation to data security, that the legally compliant implementation of data protection regulations under federal law is guaranteed within his or her office.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The FDPIC shall open an investigation into a federal body or a private person ex officio or in response to a report if there are sufficient indications that a data processing activity could violate data protection regulations.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: It may refrain from opening an investigation if the violation of data protection regulations is of minor importance.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The federal body or the private person shall provide the FDPIC with all the information and documents that is needed for the investigation. The right to refuse to provide information is governed by the Articles 16 and 17 of the APA, unless Article 50 paragraph 2 of this Act provides otherwise.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: If the data subject has filed a report, the FDPIC shall inform them about the steps taken in response and the result of any investigation.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: If the federal body or the private person fails to fulfil the duties to cooperate, the FDPIC may as part of the investigation order the following in particular:
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: Professional secrecy remains reserved.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: In order to enforce the measures under paragraph 1 the FDPIC may request support from other federal authorities and from the cantonal or communal police.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: If data protection regulations have been violated, the FDPIC may order that the processing be modified, suspended or terminated, wholly or in part, and the personal data deleted or destroyed, wholly or in part.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: It may delay or prohibit disclosure abroad if this violates the requirements of Article 16 or 17 or provisions relating to the disclosure of personal data abroad in other federal acts.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: It may in particular order that the federal body or the private person:
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: It may also order that private controllers with registered office or domicile abroad appoint a representative in accordance with Article 14.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: If the federal body or the private person has taken the required measures during the investigation in order to restore compliance with the data protection regulations, the FDPIC may simply issue an official warning.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The investigation proceedings and rulings under Articles 50 and 51 are governed by the APA.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The only party is the federal body or the private person against which or whom an investigation has been opened.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The FDPIC may contest appeal decisions of the Federal Administrative Court.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: Federal administrative authorities that supervise private persons or organisations outside the Federal Administration in accordance with another federal act shall invite the FDPIC to comment before they issue a ruling that relates to data protection issues.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: If the FDPIC is conducting his or her own investigation against the same party, the two authorities shall coordinate their proceedings.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: Federal authorities and cantonal authorities shall provide the FDPIC with the information and personal data that it requires to fulfil its statutory duties.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The FDPIC shall provide the following authorities with the information and personal data that they require to fulfil their statutory duties:
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The FDPIC may exchange information or personal data with foreign authorities that are responsible for data protection in order that they may fulfil their respective statutory duties in relation to data protection, provided the following requirements are satisfied:
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: In order to justify its request for administrative assistance or to comply with the request from an authority, the FDPIC may provide the following information in particular:
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: Before the FDPIC provides information that may include professional, trade or manufacturing secrets to a foreign authority, it shall inform the natural persons or legal entities concerned that hold these secrets, and invite them to comment, unless this is not possible or requires disproportionate effort.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The FDPIC shall keep a register of the processing activities of federal bodies. The register shall be published.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The FDPIC shall submit a report on his or her activities to the Federal Assembly every year. He or she shall submit the report to the Federal Council at the same time. The report shall be published.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: In cases of general interest, the FDPIC shall inform the public about its findings and rulings.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The FDPIC shall also carry out the following tasks in particular:
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: It may also advise federal bodies that are not subject to his or her supervision in accordance with Articles 2 and 4. The federal bodies may allow him or her to inspect files.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The FDPIC has the power to declare to foreign authorities that are responsible for data protection that direct service is permitted in relation to data protection in Switzerland, provided Switzerland is granted reciprocal rights.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The FDPIC shall charge private persons fees for:
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The Federal Council shall specify the amount of the fees.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: It may stipulate the cases in which it is possible to waive or reduce a fee.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: On complaint, a fine not exceeding 250,000 francs shall be imposed on private persons who:
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: A fine not exceeding 250,000 francs shall be imposed on private persons who, in violation of Article 49 paragraph 3, wilfully provide the FDPIC with false information or wilfully fail to cooperate in the course of an investigation.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: On complaint, a fine not exceeding 250,000 francs shall be imposed on private persons who wilfully:
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: Any person who, while practising his or her profession, acquires knowledge of secret personal data for the purpose of that profession but thereafter wilfully discloses such data shall on complaint be liable to a fine not exceeding 250,000 francs.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The same penalty shall apply to any person who wilfully discloses secret personal data that has come to his or her knowledge while carrying on an activity for or while training with a person subject to a duty of confidentiality.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The disclosure of secret personal data after ceasing to practise a profession or after completing training is also a criminal offence.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: Any private person who wilfully fails to comply with a ruling issued by the FDPIC or a decision of the appeal courts that refers to the penalty under this Article shall be liable to a fine not exceeding 250,000 francs.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The criminal liability of businesses is governed by Articles 6 and 7 of the Federal Act of 22 March 1974 on Administrative Criminal Law (ACLA).
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: If a fine not exceeding 50,000 francs is under consideration and if the identification of the perpetrators in accordance with Article 6 ACLA requires measures that would be disproportionate in view of the potential penalty, the authority may decide not to pursue these persons but instead to order the business to pay the fine (Art. 7 ACLA).
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The prosecution and the adjudication of criminal acts is a matter for the cantons.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The FDPIC may file a complaint with the competent prosecution authority and exercise the rights of a private claimant in the proceedings.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: Prosecution is subject to a statute of limitations of five years.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The Federal Council may conclude international treaties relating to:
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The repeal and the amendment of other legislation are regulated in Annex 1.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: Articles 7, 22 and 23 do not apply to data processing that began before this Act comes into force, provided the purpose of processing remains unchanged and no new data are collected.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: This Act does not apply to FDPIC investigations that are ongoing at the time that it comes into force; likewise, this Act does not apply to appeals pending against first instance decisions issued before it comes into force. Such cases are governed by the previous law.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: For federal bodies, regulations in other federal legislation that relate to personal data shall continue to apply to the data of legal entities for five years from the date on which this Act come into force. In particular federal bodies may continue to disclose the data of legal entities in accordance with Article 57s paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Government and Administration Organisation Act of 21 March 1997 for five years from the date on which this Act come into force if there is a legal basis that authorises them to disclose personal data.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The election of the Commissioner and the termination of his or her term of office shall be governed by the previous law until the end of the legislature period in which this Act comes into force.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: If the incumbent is elected in the first vote of the United Federal Assembly to elect the Commissioner, the Commissioner's new term of office begins on the day after the election.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: If the Commissioner's employment contract was based on the previous law, the previous law continues to apply.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: Coordination with other enactments is regulated in Annex 2.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: This Act is subject to an optional referendum.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf

text: The Federal Council shall determine the commencement date.
source_document: KB 2/Switzerland/Switzerland Revised Federal Act on Data Protection.pdf
